newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand asks banks to hand forex gains to govt.
newsitem.headline: Thailand asks banks to hand forex gains to govt.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand said on Wednesday it would ask commercial banks with long dollar positions to hand over to the government any foreign exchange gains arising from its decision to float the baht.

Central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said at a press conference: "For commercial banks making foreign exchange gains from long dollar positions, they are required to sell them to authorities, i.e. their foreign exchange gains should be returned to the state."
The governor said the government kept unchanged a current maximum net dollar position limit that Thai-based commercial banks can maintain.
The limit is a maximum of 15 percent of total bank liabilities and 20 percent of their assets.
Analysts said the governor's statement was designed to curb any moves by commercial banks to profit from foreign exchange volatility by hoarding dollars.
